titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§43–54: Bodonchar's Descendants
about: Twelve sections of descent: Bodončar's sons, and the sons of Qabiči and the other lines, down to the generation that leads to Yesügei, with the clan names that each line gave rise to. The text is almost entirely one frame, 'X's son, Y name-having, there-was' (genitive + köġün + neretü büleġe), and the clan names follow the same pattern: a reason ending in tula 'because', then oboγtan boluba 'clan-having became'. Read it for the genitives (-un, -ün, -(n)u, -(n)ü, -jin: the Ming 的), the possessives -tü / -tei / -tu / -tan (有的), the plurals in -d / -s (每), and the participles that tell a story in miniature: the Tatars' seizing of Ambaγai Qaγan, his two messages from the Kitad's custody, and Jesügei's meeting with a Merkid bridegroom and his bride on the Onan. Where I could not construe a form with confidence the note says so; the least certain places are §46's reasons for the Barula and Adargin clans, §50's Belgütei aside, and the messages in §53.

sentences.t: Bodončar-un ablin eme-dēče töregsen Barim-Siġiratu-Qabiči neretü büleġe.
sentences.l: Bodončar's, own-wed wife-from born, Barim-Siġiratu-Qabiči name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Born to Bodonchar by his own wedded wife was a son named Barim-Sigiratu-Qabichi.
sentences.n: From here to §54 nearly every unit is genealogy, and one frame carries it: [X-of] köġün [Y] neretü büleġe, 'X's son, Y name-having, there-was'. Learn its parts and the page reads itself. The genitive (-un, -ün, -(n)u, -(n)ü, -jin) is the Ming's 的 'of'; neretü / neretei is 'name-having', the possessive -tü / -tei (Ming 有的); büleġe is 'there was' (Ming 有來). eme-dēče 'from the wife' is the ablative -dēče (Ming 處 'place', so 'from the place of the wife'): a child 'born from' a mother. I cannot analyse ablin (Ming 自娶的 'self-married'); perhaps ab- 'take' with an ending. I keep the Ming's sense, 'own wedded', which sets this wife against the concubine of the next unit. Barim-Siġiratu-Qabiči is one name (Ming 兒名 'son's name'); from the next unit he is called Qabiči.

sentences.t: Tere Qabiči-Baγ̇atur-un eke-jin inže iregsen-i Bodončar tatažu büleġe.
sentences.l: That Qabiči-Baγ̇atur's mother's dowry-accompanying coming-one (acc.), Bodončar concubine-making, there-was.
sentences.i: Bodonchar had taken as a concubine the woman who had come as a dowry attendant with the mother of Qabichi-Ba'atur.
sentences.n: Tere ... iregsen-i is a noun phrase built up before its verb: 'that — of Qabiči-Baγ̇atur the mother's — dowry-attendant — the one who came (accusative)'. iregsen is ire- 'come' + the past participle -gsen 'the one who has come' (Ming 來了的), and the -i makes her the object of tatažu. inže (Ming 從嫁 'married along with') is a person who comes with a bride; 'dowry attendant' is my word for it. tatažu is tata- 'pull, draw' as a converb; the Ming glosses it 做妾着 'making a concubine', and I follow the Ming, not the dictionary sense of tata-, which I do not see giving this. The Ming (母) marks eke-jin 'mother's' with brackets: it is Qabiči's own mother, the wedded wife of the last unit, and the concubine is the woman who arrived in her train.

sentences.l: One son was-born.
sentences.i: A son was born.
sentences.n: törebe is töre- 'be born' + past -be (front-vowel form), Ming 生了. The concubine of the last unit is the mother, but the words do not say so; nothing here is the Ming's 'to her'. nigen 'one' (Ming 一箇 'one item') is the number 'a'.

sentences.l: Žeġüredei name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: He was named Jeguredei.
sentences.n: The same frame as the first unit, neretü büleġe, now without a genitive: the name follows the subject directly. Žeġüredei is the root of the clan name Žeġüreid in §44.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [part of 名字有的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Žeġüredei, formerly, the žügeli-into entering, there-was.
sentences.i: Jeguredei had earlier been in the jügeli.
sentences.n: žügeli is the Ming's 以竿懸肉祭天 'hang meat on a pole and sacrifice to Heaven': a sacrificial pole, or the rite itself. §44 drives Jeguredei out 'from the žügeli', so it must be a rite or company that one can belong to or be shut out of; 'been in' is my reading of oron büleġe, oro- 'enter' as a converb + 'was' (Ming 入 有來). urida 'formerly' (Ming 在前). -dür is the dative-locative 'in, into'.

morph.gloss: the žügeli: a pole on which meat was hung as an offering to Heaven, or the rite itself (Ming 以竿懸肉祭天) [以竿懸肉祭天]
dative-locative: in, into (front-vowel form) [part of 以竿懸肉祭天]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Bodončar without having-become's, after,
sentences.i: After Bodonchar was no more,
sentences.n: ügei 'without, none' (Ming 無) + boluγsan-u 'of the one who has become' (Ming 做了的): 'of his having become nothing', and I take it as 'was gone, was no more'. The Ming does not say 'died' and I do not either. qoina 'after' (Ming 後頭 'behind') closes the time clause.

morph.gloss: past participle: the one who has become [part of 做了 的]

sentences.t: tere Žeġüredei-ji ger daluγ̇a Adaṅqa Urjaṅqadai küġün aluγ̇a.
sentences.l: that Žeġüredei (acc.) house constantly, Adaṅqa Urjaṅqadai man dwelt.
sentences.i: a man of the Adanqa, Uriangqadai, lived on constantly in the house with Jeguredei.
sentences.n: Žeġüredei-ji ends in the accusative -ji, but the Ming writes 行, which also marks 'to, with'; as 'dwelt' takes no object I read 'with'. This is a guess: the words do not say who kept the household. Adaṅqa is the Ming's 種名 'tribe-name' and Urjaṅqadai its 姓氏 'clan-name'; I read them together as 'the Adaṅqa man Urjaṅqadai', with küġün 'man' as the head (the -dai ending I cannot place, as in the glossary). aluγ̇a is a- 'dwell' + the back-vowel past -luγ̇a, the partner of -leġe in büleġe (Ming 住來). daluγ̇a (Ming 常川 'regularly') I cannot analyse.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also 'he, she' (demonstrative and third-person pronoun) [那]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel); the Ming writes 行 [行]
Adaṅqa (Adanqa), a tribe or clan name [種名]
Urjaṅqadai (Uriangqadai), a man of the Uriangqai (the suffix uncertain) [姓氏(名)]
past narrative: used to dwell (back-vowel form) [part of 住來]

sentences.l: Of-him-belonging, is, indeed, saying,
sentences.i: “He is that man's,” they said,
sentences.n: The speaker and the 'he' are not written. The Ming has 他的 有 者 說着 'his, is, indeed, saying'. Teġün-ü-ġei is tere (stem teġün-) + genitive -ü + -ġei, 'belonging to', as in the published §18, where the glossary marks it uncertain. My reading: the kinsmen are declaring that Jeguredei belongs to the Adanqa man, not to Bodonchar. That rests on the next unit, which expels him, not on these words. bi is the Ming's 有 'is' (not the pronoun 'I'), že the particle 'indeed'.

morph.gloss: that, that one; teġün- is its stem before a case ending [他]
belonging to, 'his own' (uncertain) [part of 他的]
is, exists (verb; perhaps a short form of bü-); not the pronoun 'I' here, for the Ming has 有 [有]

sentences.l: The žügeli-from driving-out, Žeġüreid clan-having making-become,
sentences.i: Having driven him out of the jügeli, they made him a Jegüreid, with a clan of his own,
sentences.n: A converb chain whose subject is unwritten: 'they' (the kin) is my supply. γarγažu is γar- 'go out' + causative -γa- + -žu, 'making go out', Ming 逐出着 'driving out'. bolγažu is bol- + the same causative, 'making become' (Ming 敎做着 'cause to be'). oboγtu 'clan-having' is the possessive -tu again (Ming 姓有的). Žeġüreid is Žeġüredei's name with the plural -d, a group-name (Ming 一種(名)). The chain continues in the next unit, split here to keep the units short.

morph.gloss: the žügeli: pole-and-meat offering to Heaven, or the rite itself (Ming 以竿懸肉祭天) [以竿懸肉祭天]
causative: make ... (here: drive out) [part of 逐出着]
the Žeġüreid (Jegüreid), a group name built on Žeġüredei with plural -d [一種(名)]
possessive: having, provided with (back-vowel form) [part of 姓有的]
causative: make become [part of 敎做 着]

sentences.l: Žered's ancestor, that-one became.
sentences.i: and he became the ancestor of the Jered.
sentences.n: Žered-ün 'of the Žered' (genitive -ün after r; Ming 一種(名)的), ebüge 'ancestor' (Ming 祖), tere 'he', boluba 'became'. The people were Žeġüreid in the last unit and are Žered here. The Ming glosses both 一種(名) and I do not know whether Shiratori's two spellings mean one name; I take them as one.

morph.gloss: the Žered (Jered), a group name (perhaps the same as Žeġüreid) [一種(名)]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
that, that one; also 'he, she' (demonstrative and third-person pronoun) [那]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Qabiči-Baγ̇atur's son Menen-Tudun there-was.
sentences.i: Qabichi-Ba'atur had a son, Menen-Tudun.
sentences.n: The frame again, with the Ming's (兒)名 'son's name' before each name to tell the reader that a name is coming, and 勇士 'brave man' for baγ̇atur, which stands in names as well as for 'hero'. The Ming says nothing more of Menen-Tudun.

morph.gloss: Qabiči-Baγ̇atur (Qabichi the Brave), the son of §43 [(人)名 勇士]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.t: Menen-Tudun-(n)u köġün Qači-Külüg, Qačin, Qačiγ̇u, Qačula, Qačiγ̇un, Qarandai, Način-Baγ̇atur doloγ̇an büleġe.
sentences.l: Menen-Tudun's son Qači-Külüg, Qačin, Qačiγ̇u, Qačula, Qačiγ̇un, Qarandai, Način-Baγ̇atur, seven there-were.
sentences.i: Menen-Tudun's sons were Qachi-Külüg, Qachin, Qachi'u, Qachula, Qachi'un, Qarandai and Nachin-Ba'atur: seven.
sentences.n: Seven names, one list, kept whole as Shiratori's commas give it. köġün is singular ('son') yet seven names follow and doloγ̇an 'seven' counts them, so köġün is a collective here (the plural köġüd comes in the following units). Five of the seven names begin Qači-: the Ming has only (兒)名 for each, so I can say nothing about how they are related.

morph.gloss: Način-Baγ̇atur (Nachin the Brave), a son's name [(兒)名 勇士]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.t: Qači-Külüg-ün köġün Qaidu, Nomolun eke-dēče töregsen büleġe.
sentences.l: Qači-Külüg's son Qaidu, Nomolun mother-from born, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi-Külüg's son was Qaidu, born of a mother named Nomolun.
sentences.n: Nomolun is the Ming's 婦人名 'woman's name', and eke-dēče 'from the mother' (ablative, Ming 處) gives her as his mother. The Ming glosses each name as simply (兒)名 'son's name'; Qaidu has no further comment here.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
past participle: the one born [part of 生了的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Qačin's son Nojagidai name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachin's son was named Noyagidai.
sentences.n: The plain frame. neretei is nere + -tei, the front-vowel possessive that elsewhere appears as -tü (neretü); the Ming has 名字有的 in both. I cannot give the rule that chooses between the two forms.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [part of 名字有的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.t: Nojansiγ aburitu tula Nojakin oboγtan boluba.
sentences.l: Noyan-like temper-having because, Nojakin clan-having became.
sentences.i: Because of their lordly temper, they became the clan called Noyakin.
sentences.n: This is the first of many clan-name explanations, each built the same way: a reason ending in tula 'because' (Ming 上頭), then oboγtan boluba 'became clan-having'. Nojansiγ is the Ming's 裝官人 'one who puts on the official's manner': I read nojan 'lord' + a -siγ 'resembling' ending, from the Ming, not from the word. aburitu is aburi 'disposition' + -tu (Ming 性兒有的). The subject is unwritten; 'they' I supply, and I take it to be Nojagidai's people. The clan name Nojakin sounds like nojan, and I take that to be the point, but the Ming does not say it.

morph.gloss: resembling, putting on the manner of (the Ming 裝 'put on, feign'; uncertain) [part of 裝官人]
disposition, temper (Ming 性兒 'nature') [性兒有的]
possessive: having, provided with (back-vowel form) [part of 性兒有的]
because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of', hence 'for that reason') [上頭]
the Nojakin (Noyakin), a clan name [一種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Qačiγ̇u's son Barulatai name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi'u's son was named Barulatai.
sentences.n: Printed Qačiγ̇-jin; the Han (兀 = γ̇u) shows the stem is Qačiγ̇u, so Shiratori's print drops the u before -jin, and I read the stem whole. barulatai (a name) will turn out to be near the clan names Barula and Barulas below, and I do not claim the link, since the Ming only says 名字有的.

morph.gloss: Qačiγ̇u (Qachi'u), a man's name (printed without the final u) [(人)名]
possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [part of 名字有的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Big body-having, food-at mighty, there-was.
sentences.i: He was big of body, and fierce at his food.
sentences.n: bejetü is beje 'body' + -tü (Ming 身子有的). ideġen-e is ideġen 'food' + the dative-locative -e (Ming 茶飯行), so 'at food', and baruγ is the Ming's 猛的 'fierce, mighty'. 'Fierce at his food' is the literal sense; I understand it as a great eater, which the next lines make the reason for a clan name, but that is my reading. baruγ is also the root of Barula, Barulas, the clan name.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [part of 身子有的]
fierce, mighty, brave (root of Barula) [猛的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.l: Barulas clan-having became.
sentences.i: They became the clan called Barulas.
sentences.n: Barulas is Barula + the plural -s (Ming 每), a clan name. The subject is unwritten. I link Barula to baruγ in the last unit; the Ming does not.

morph.gloss: the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [一種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Qačula's son food-at mighty because,
sentences.i: Because Qachula's son was fierce at his food,
sentences.n: A reason without its result, which follows in the next two units; I have cut the long sentence here so each unit holds one thought. ideġen-e baruγ is as before. Notice that this is a second son of a second man (Qačula, not Qačiγ̇u) to be given the same reason: the passage does not explain the repetition, and I can only report it.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of', hence 'for that reason') [上頭]

sentences.t: Jeke-Barula, Üčügen-Barula nereidčü Barulas oboγtan bolγažu
sentences.l: Great-Barula, Little-Barula naming, Barulas clan-having making-become,
sentences.i: naming them Great Barula and Little Barula, they made them the clan called Barulas,
sentences.n: nereidčü is nere 'name' + a verb-forming -id- (uncertain) + the converb -čü (Ming 名字喚着 'calling by name'); the -d- shows up before -čü as in uduridču (§54). jeke / üčügen are 'great / small' (Ming 大 / 小). The subject is unwritten; 'they' is my supply. bolγažu is bol- + causative -γa- + -žu (Ming 做着), the same pattern as in §44.

morph.gloss: Jeke-Barula (Great Barula), a branch of the Barula [大 種名]
Üčügen-Barula (Little Barula), a branch of the Barula [小 種名]
verb-former: to name (uncertain) [part of 名字喚着]
converb after a consonant: -ing [part of 名字喚着]
the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
causative: make become [part of 做着]

sentences.t: Erdemtü-Barula, Tödöġen-Barula teriġüten Barulas tede boluba.
sentences.l: Erdemtü-Barula, Tödöġen-Barula, head-having-ones (Ming: kinds), Barulas, those became.
sentences.i: Those became the Barulas, with Erdemtü-Barula and Tödö'en-Barula as their heads.
sentences.n: teriġüten is the doubtful word: teriġü 'head' + the plural possessive -ten 'those having', Ming 項每. 項 can be 'neck' or 'item, kind', so either 'the headed ones, the chiefs' or 'the branches' (so: 'the Barulas in the branches Erdemtü-Barula and Tödö'en-Barula'). I chose 'heads'. The clause closes with the usual tede boluba, 'those became' (Ming 那的 做了).

morph.gloss: Erdemtü-Barula, a branch of the Barula (erdem 'skill' + -tü?; uncertain) [一種 (名)]
Tödöġen-Barula, a branch of the Barula [一種 (名)]
the Barula (Barulas), a clan name [種(名)]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.t: Qarandai-jin köġüd budaγ̇an qudqulaqu eki teriġü ügeġün tula
sentences.l: Qarandai's sons, porridge stirring, brain-head without-ones, because,
sentences.i: Because the sons of Qarandai stirred porridge and had no brains in their heads,
sentences.n: Another reason. budaγ̇an qudqulaqu is 'porridge, the stirring one' (Ming 粥飯 攪的): qudqula- 'stir' + the participle -qu. eki teriġü is the Ming's 腦 頭 'brain, head', then ügeġün 'those without' (Ming 無的每): I take 'brain-head' as 'wits' and the whole as an insult. The clan name in the next unit, Budaγ̇ad, looks like budaγ̇an 'porridge'; that is probably the point, though the Ming does not say so. ügeġün I read as ügei + a plural -ġün, as in the glossary.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of', hence 'for that reason') [上頭]

sentences.l: Budaγ̇ad clan-having, those became.
sentences.i: they became the clan called Buda'ad.
sentences.n: Budaγ̇ad (Ming 一種(名) 'a kind of ...') is a clan name with the plural -d, built on budaγ̇an 'porridge' if the last unit is right. I keep it as a single name.

morph.gloss: the Budaγ̇ad (Buda'ad), a clan name; compare budaγ̇an 'porridge' [一種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un's son Adarkidai name-having, there-was.
sentences.i: Qachi'un's son was named Adarkidai.
sentences.n: The plain frame; after the stem Qačiγ̇un (ending in n) the genitive is -(n)u.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [part of 名字有的]
past narrative: there was, used to be (front-vowel form) [part of 有來]

sentences.t: Aqa deġü žaγ̇ura adaluγči tula Adargin oboγtan bolba.
sentences.l: Elder-brother younger-brother between, adaluγči because, Adargin clan-having became.
sentences.i: Because he was a spy between elder and younger brother, they became the clan called Adargin.
sentences.n: adaluγči is the doubtful word: the Ming gives 間謀, 'spy, one who sows discord' (間 'between' + 謀 'plot'), and it seems to end in the agent -či, but I cannot find the stem. 'Spy' is the Ming; 'sower of discord' the sense I think it carries. aqa deġü 'elder brother, younger brother' (Ming 兄 弟) with žaγ̇ura 'between' (Ming 間) is the setting. Whose brothers they are, and who 'he' is, the words do not say: the unit follows Adarkidai's, and I take him. The clan name Adargin may echo Adarkidai; the Ming does not make that link.

morph.gloss: a spy, one who sows discord (Ming 間謀); stem uncertain, ending perhaps agent -či [間謀]
because of, on account of (postposition; Ming 上頭 'on top of', hence 'for that reason') [上頭]
the Adargin, a clan name [一種(名)]
possessive, plural: having [part of 姓 (有的)每]
past tense (back-vowel form) [part of 做了]

sentences.t: Način-Baγ̇atur-un köġüd Uruγ̇udai, Monγutai nereten büleġe.
sentences.l: Način-Baγ̇atur's sons Uruγ̇udai, Monγutai names-having, there-were.
sentences.i: Nachin-Ba'atur's sons were named Uru'udai and Mongqutai.
sentences.n: The frame with plural köġüd 'sons' (Ming 兒子每) and nereten, the plural 'having names'. The two names are the roots of the clan names in the next unit.

sentences.n: ökin 'daughter' (Ming 女) stands without an ending as the object of ögčü 'giving' (ög- + -čü, Ming 與着). The giving is a marriage: the next unit says he himself took her.

morph.gloss: converb after a consonant: giving [part of 與着]

sentences.l: Himself, own-daughter escorting, going being,
sentences.i: and was going himself, escorting his own daughter,
sentences.n: öġesün is the Ming's 自己 'oneself', emphatic: he himself. ökin(i)-jen is 'his own daughter' (ökin + the reflexive -(i)jen, Ming 女子 自的行, with Shiratori's bracketed (i)). hüdežü is hüde- 'see off, escort' (Ming 送著; the sense of a bride's escort is my gloss), odqu is od- 'go' + the participle -qu, and bolun the converb of bol- 'be, become', Ming 做了: 'being a-going', so I read 'was on his way'.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (front-vowel form) [自的行]
to see off, escort (Ming 送) [送著︀]

sentences.t: Tatar Žüin irgen Ambaγai Qaγan-(n)i barižu
sentences.l: Tatar Žüin people, Ambaγai Qaγan (acc.) seizing,
sentences.i: the Tatar people, the Jüyin, seized Ambaqai Qahan
sentences.n: Tatar and Žüin are the Ming's 種名 and 種姓(名), two labels for one people, and I take them in apposition, 'the Tatar, the Žüin people'. Qaγan-(n)i is the accusative (Ming 行) and the object of barižu 'seizing' (bari- 'take hold', Ming 拿著). The subject is the Tatar; their act is told in a converb, and the main verb comes some units later.

morph.gloss: the Žüin (Jüyin), a people (Ming 種姓(名)) [種姓(名)]
to take hold of, seize [拿著︀]

sentences.l: Kitad's Altan Qaγan-to taking, going-at,
sentences.i: and as they were taking him to Altan Qahan of the Kitad,
sentences.n: Kitad-un is the Ming's 契丹的 'of the Kitan', and Altan Qaγan its 金皇帝 'Jin emperor': Altan means 'gold' and renders the Jin dynasty's name, so the ruler of the northern empire is meant. abču is ab- 'take' + -ču (Ming 將著 'taking along'); odqui-dur is od- 'go' + the participle -qui + -dur, 'at the going' (Ming 去的 時, 'when going'). The subject is still the Tatar.

morph.gloss: the Kitad (Ming 契丹 'Kitan'), the northern peoples under the Jin [契丹]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
gold; here the Jin emperor's title (Ming 金) [金]

sentences.t: Ambaγai Qaγan Besütei küġün Balaγači elčin(i)-ġer ügüležü ilerün
sentences.l: Ambaγai Qaγan, Besütei man Balaγači envoy-by speaking, sending,
sentences.i: Ambaqai Qahan sent word by an envoy, Balaqachi of the Besütei, saying:
sentences.n: Besütei is the Ming's 姓氏(名) 'clan name' here, but in §47 it was a man's name; the clan grew from the man. Balaγači (人名). elčin(i)-ġer is the Ming's 使臣行 敎 'to the envoy, cause': the envoy is the instrument, -ġer an instrumental (cf. -ber), with Shiratori's (i). ügüležü is ügüle- 'speak' + -žü; ilerün is ile- 'send' + -rün, Ming 去. I take ile- 'send' from the Ming's 'go'; the form could also be a motion verb. The chain breaks off at the colon of the next units: two messages follow, to Qutula and to Qadaγan-Taiši.

morph.gloss: the Besütei, a clan (here Ming 姓氏 'surname'; the man's name in §47) [姓氏(名)]
envoy, messenger (elči with n; the (i) is Shiratori's) [使臣行]
to send (the Ming has 去 'go') [去]
converb of time: when -ing (front-vowel form) [part of 去]

sentences.t: Qabul Qaγan-(n)u doloγ̇an köġüd-ün dundatu Qutula-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Qabul Qaγan's seven sons' middle-one Qutula-to, speaking:
sentences.i: To Qutula, the middle one of the seven sons of Qabul Qahan, saying:
sentences.n: dundatu is dunda 'middle' + -tu 'having', Ming 中間的 'the middle one'; Qutula is fourth in the §48 list of seven, which fits. köġüd-ün is 'of the sons' (plural -d + genitive -ün; Ming 兒子的). Qutula-da is the dative-locative -da (Ming 行) after a vowel. ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün 'while speaking' (Ming 說); the colon is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
converb of time: while speaking (front-vowel form) [part of 說]

sentences.t: harban köġüd-ün dotora Qadaγ̇an-Taiši-da ügüle keġen ügüležü ilerün:
sentences.l: Ten sons' among, Qadaγ̇an-Taiši-to say! saying, speaking, sending:
sentences.i: “Among the ten sons, say to Qadaqan-Taishi!” he said, and sent word:
sentences.n: Whose ten sons? The Ming has only 十箇兒子的內 'among the ten sons', and I cannot tell whether the ten belong to Qabul, to Qutula or to someone else; the speaker may be ordering the message passed to a second man. ügüle without an ending is the bare stem, 'say!' (Ming 說); keġen 'saying' closes the quotation (Ming 麽道). Qadaγ̇an-Taiši: taiši is a title, 'prince' (from Chinese 太子), as in Negün-Taiši above.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
Qadaγ̇an-Taiši (Qadaqan-Taishi), a man's name; taiši 'prince' [(人)名]
converb: saying (closes a quotation) [part of 麽道]
to send (the Ming has 去 'go') [去]
converb of time: when -ing (front-vowel form) [part of 去]

sentences.l: All's Qaγan, realm's lord having-become,
sentences.i: “I, who became the Qahan of all and lord of the realm,
sentences.n: The speech begins here: Shiratori's opening quote is in the first word, and the closing one after soridqun. Qamuγ-un Qaγan is 'Qaγan of all' (Ming 普的皇帝; compare Qamuγ Monγol, 'all Mongols'), ulus-un ežen 'lord of the realm' (Ming 國(的)主人). bolužu is bolu- 'become' + -žu (Ming 做著). The first person is not written: the Mongol says only 'having become'.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [(的)]

sentences.l: Daughter-my-own, himself, sending-my-own, me-by, be-warned!
sentences.i: —seeing off my own daughter myself—take warning from me!
sentences.n: A packed line, and I give it as I read it. öki-ben (Ming 女子 自的行) is 'my own daughter' (öki, the front-vowel variant of ökin, + the reflexive -ben); öġesün 'oneself'; hüdeküi-ben 'my own seeing-off' (hüde- + the participle -küi + -ben), so 'in my own sending-off of my daughter'. nama-γ̇ar is 'by me': Shiratori prints mama-, but the Han (納馬) reads na-ma, so it is bi, stem nama-, with -γ̇ar (Ming 行), an instrumental. kesedkün is kese- 'warn' (Ming 戒) + the plural-addressed imperative (Ming 您 'you'): 'take warning, you'.

morph.gloss: to see off, escort (Ming 送) [送]
I; nama- is its stem before a case ending [我]
to take warning, be warned (Ming 戒) [戒]

sentences.l: Tatar people-by was-seized.
sentences.i: I was seized by the Tatar people.
sentences.n: bariγdaγ̇a is bari- 'seize' + the passive -γda- (as in toγ̇aγda- of §24) + a past ending -γ̇a (Ming 被拿了 'was seized'; the ending is uncertain). The dative -e on irgen-e (Ming 行) stands for 'by' with a passive.

morph.gloss: to seize, take hold of [被拿了]

sentences.l: I five fingers-my-own nails bare-until,
sentences.i: Until the nails of my five fingers are bare,
sentences.n: A parallel pair of 'until' clauses, in -tala (as in atala, §24): tamutala 'until bare' (Ming 禿了; tamu- is a stem I cannot identify) and, next, qaγ̇udtala 'until worn away'. quruγ̇ud(i)-jan is 'my own fingers' (quruγun, 'finger', + the plural -d + the reflexive -(i)jan; Ming 指頭 自的行), and kimül 'fingernail' (Ming 指甲). Note the ‘I’ (bi) is written here, not before.

morph.gloss: finger (Ming 指頭) [指頭 自的行]
plural [part of 指頭 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (back-vowel form) [自的行]
to be bare, worn bare (Ming 禿了; stem uncertain) [禿了]

sentences.l: Ten fingers-my-own, worn-away-until,
sentences.i: until my ten fingers are worn away,
sentences.n: qaγ̇udtala is qaγ̇ud- 'be worn out, ground away' (Ming 磨盡了 'worn to nothing') + -tala. Together with the last unit it is an oath of effort: to the last of nail and finger, try.

morph.gloss: finger (Ming 指頭) [指頭 自的行]
plural [part of 指頭 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own, with the accusative i (back-vowel form) [自的行]
to be worn out, ground away (Ming 磨盡了) [磨盡了]

sentences.l: Enmity my-of repaying, try!”
sentences.i: try to repay my enmity!”
sentences.n: hači is the Ming's 讎, ‘enmity, revenge’ (an enemy or a feud). min-u 'my' follows its noun (bi, stem min-, + -u). aburan is abura- 'repay, requite' (Ming 報) + the converb -n. soridqun is sori- 'try, test' (Ming 試) + -d- + -qun, a plural-address imperative, as in kesedkün above (the Ming 您). The closing quote mark is part of the word as printed.

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance, a feud (Ming 讎) [讎]
I; min- is its stem before the genitive [我]
genitive: of (here set after its noun: my) [的]

sentences.l: Saying, sent.
sentences.i: So saying, he sent word.
sentences.n: keġežu is keġe- 'say' + -žu (printed -žu, not -žü, though the stem is front-vowel; the Ming has 說著 regardless). iležüġü is ile- 'send' + the past narrative -žüġü (Ming 去了有來 'went'): the Ming reads it as the messenger going. I read 'sent word' for the verb that ilerün also needs. The message ends here, and §54 begins a new scene.

morph.gloss: to send (the Ming has 去 'go') [去了有來]
past narrative: sent, went (front-vowel form) [part of 去了有來]

sentences.t: Tere čaγ-tur Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Onan müren-(n)e šibaγ̇ulan jabuqui-dur
sentences.l: That time-at Jesügei-Baγ̇atur Onan river-at hawk-flying going-when,
sentences.i: At that time, when Yesügei-Ba'atur was out flying hawks by the river Onan,
sentences.n: A time clause ending in -qui-dur (jabuqui-dur, Ming 行的 時分, 'at the going'), hung on čaγ-tur 'at the time'. Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Ming (人)名) is the man of §50; Onan, müren-(n)e 'at the river' (Ming 河名, 河處). šibaγ̇ulan is the Ming's 放鷹 'fly hawks': I take it as šibaγ̇u 'bird' + -la- 'hunt with' + the converb -n, but the stem is not otherwise known to me. 'Out' is the sense of jabu- 'walk, go about'.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at (back-vowel form) [part of 時分]
Jesügei-Baγ̇atur (Yesügei the Brave), a man's name [(人)名]
the Onan, a river (the Onon) [河名]
to hunt with a hawk, fly hawks (Ming 放鷹; stem uncertain) [放鷹]
dative-locative: at the time of [時分]

sentences.t: Merkid-ün Jeke-Čiledü Olqunuγ̇ud irgen-eče öki abču eġüsgežü aisuqu-ji
sentences.l: Merkid's Jeke-Čiledü, Olqunuγ̇ud people-from, girl taking, wife-taking, coming (acc.),
sentences.i: Yeke-Chiledü of the Merkid had taken a girl from the Olqunu'ud people to wed, and was coming home with her;
sentences.n: Merkid-ün is the Merkid with the genitive (Ming 種名(的)). Jeke-Čiledü is a man (Ming (人)名), irgen-eče 'from the people' (ablative -eče, Ming 處). abču eġüsgežü: two converbs, 'taking, taking as wife' (Ming 要着, 取著); eġüsge- is the Ming's 取 and I take it to mean 'wed'. aisuqu-ji 'the coming (him, accusative)' (Ming 來的行) is the object of 'meeting' in the next unit, so Jeke-Čiledü is described first and met next; the subject of the whole chain is Jesügei, carried over from the last unit.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [(的)]
to take (a wife), to wed (Ming 取) [取著︀]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]

sentences.l: Meeting, peering, look-if,
sentences.i: He met them as they came, peered closer, and when he looked,
sentences.n: Another chain whose subject (Jesügei) is not written. žoluγa- is 'meet' (Ming 遇); öngeižü, Ming 探著 'spy out, peer into', I cannot analyse, and it looks like önge 'colour' in the next unit although the Ming glosses them differently; üžeġesü is üže- 'see' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 看呵, 'if / when he looked'), which sets up what he sees.

morph.gloss: to peer in, look closely (Ming 探; stem uncertain, perhaps related to önge) [探著︀]

sentences.t: önge žisü bušitai öki qatud üžežü
sentences.l: Colour, hue other-having girl, ladies seeing,
sentences.i: he saw that the girl, of uncommon looks, was a lady,
sentences.n: önge žisü is the Ming's 顏 色 'complexion, colour', a pair of near-synonyms; bušitai is buši 'other, different' + the possessive -tai (Ming 別有的 'otherwise-having'), so 'of looks other than common'. qatud is qatun 'lady' with plural -d (Ming 婦人(每) 'women'), and the words do not tell me whether it names the girl ('a lady') or sits in apposition ('the girl, the ladies'). I read 'a lady'.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (back-vowel form) [有的]
lady, a woman of rank (Ming 婦人 'woman') [婦人]

sentences.l: Home-to-his-own back running,
sentences.i: and ran back to his own home,
sentences.n: ger-tür(i)-jen is 'to his own home' (ger + dative -tür + the reflexive -jen; Shiratori's (i); Ming 家 自的行). qarin is the Ming's 回 'back'; qaγ̇lžu its 奔著 'rushing', with a stem qaγ̇l- I cannot place. The subject is Jesügei, and he runs home, so I read that he will fetch his brothers; the words say only that he sees, then runs.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: to, at (the (i) is Shiratori's) [part of 家 自的行]
to run, rush (Ming 奔; stem uncertain) [奔著︀]

sentences.t: Negün-Taiši aqa-juγ̇an Daritai-Ödčigin deġü-ben uduridču irežüġü.
sentences.l: Negün-Taiši his-own-elder-brother, Daritai-Ödčigin his-own-younger-brother, leading, came.
sentences.i: Leading his elder brother Negün-Taishi and his younger brother Daritai-Ödchigin, he came back.
sentences.n: Negün-Taiši and Daritai-Ödčigin are Jesügei's brothers in the §50 list. aqa-juγ̇an 'his own elder brother' and deġü-ben 'his own younger brother' both carry the reflexive (Ming 自的行), which refers to the subject, Jesügei. uduridču is uduri- 'lead' + -dču, a form of -žu with the d of the stem (as in nereidčü). irežüġü is ire- 'come' + the past narrative -žüġü (Ming 來了). The part stops here, in the middle of the story.

morph.gloss: Negün-Taiši (Negün-Taishi), a man's name; taiši 'prince' [人名]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form, after a vowel) [自的行]
converb: -ing (a form of -žu; the d is unexplained) [part of 引着]
past narrative: came (front-vowel form) [part of 來了]
